metadata.title: Create Pydantic Models for Data Structures

story.iWant: define all data models used throughout the application
story.soThat: I have type safety and validation for all data
story.tasks: - Create models directory structure (AC: #1-5) - Create `/src/bet_bot/models/` directory - Create `/src/bet_bot/models/__init__.py` and export all models - Verify directory exists and is importable - Implement fixtures.py models (AC: #1, #6, #7, #8) - Create `League` model (league_id, league_name, league_country, league_season) - Create `Team` model (id, name, form data, goals, injury list reference) - Create `Fixture` model (fixture_id, kickoff_time, home_team, away_team, league, odds dict, h2h history list) - Add validators: ID fields non-empty, fixture_date must be valid ISO 8601, teams must be different - Add docstrings to all classes and fields - Add example values to model Config class - Implement form.py models (AC: #2, #6, #7, #8) - Create `RecentResult` model (result: W/D/L, opponent, goals_for, goals_against, date) - Create `TeamForm` model (team_id, team_name, last_5_results, last_10_results, win percentages, goals avg home/away) - Add validators: Results must be W/D/L, win percentages 0.0-1.0, goals >= 0 - Add docstrings explaining form tracking purpose - Add example values - Implement injuries.py models (AC: #3, #6, #7, #8) - Create `InjuredPlayer` model (player_id, player_name, position, injury_status, impact_severity) - Create `Injury` model (team_id, injured_players list, missing_key_players_count, missing_key_players_list) - Add validators: Status must be one of Doubt/Injured/Suspended/Out, impact one of Key/Moderate/Minor - Add docstrings explaining injury impact on analysis - Add example values - Implement odds.py models (AC: #4, #6, #7, #8) - Create `Market` model (market_type, odds dict mapping {outcome: float odds}) - Create `Odds` model (fixture_id, bookmaker_name, odds_updated_at, markets list) - Add validators: Odds >= 1.0, market_type non-empty, timestamp valid ISO 8601 - Add docstrings explaining market types (match_result, total_goals, corners, cards) - Add example values with realistic odds - Implement analysis.py models (AC: #5, #6, #7, #8) - Create `MarketAnalysis` model (market_type, ai_probability: 0.0-1.0, reasoning: str, confidence: 0-100) - Create `AIAnalysis` model (fixture_id, markets list, analysis_timestamp) - Create `Pick` model (fixture_id, market, ai_probability, implied_probability, ev_percentage, confidence, recommended_stake, suggested_odds) - Add validators: Probabilities 0.0-1.0, confidence 0-100, EV can be negative, odds >= 1.0 - Add docstrings explaining AI analysis flow - Add example values with realistic analysis data - Export all models from __init__.py (AC: #9) - Update `/src/bet_bot/models/__init__.py` to import and re-export all models - Test: `from bet_bot.models import Fixture, Team, League, ...` works - Verify no circular imports - Create comprehensive unit tests (AC: #9, #10) - Create `/tests/unit/test_models.py` - Test valid instances can be created for each model - Test invalid data raises ValidationError (empty IDs, invalid enums, out-of-range values) - Test model serialization to JSON and deserialization from JSON - Test Field alias support for API response mapping - Target 95%+ code coverage on models module

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Create `/src/bet_bot/models/fixtures.py` with `Fixture`, `Team`, `League` models 2. Create `/src/bet_bot/models/form.py` with `TeamForm`, `RecentResult` models 3. Create `/src/bet_bot/models/injuries.py` with `InjuredPlayer`, `Injury` models 4. Create `/src/bet_bot/models/odds.py` with `Odds`, `Market` models 5. Create `/src/bet_bot/models/analysis.py` with `AIAnalysis`, `MarketAnalysis`, `Pick` models 6. All models use Pydantic with proper validation 7. Models include docstrings explaining fields 8. Add example values to each model 9. All models can be imported without error 10. Can create instances with valid data and invalid data raises validation errors

constraint.title: Pydantic Version and Pattern
constraint.description: Project uses Pydantic v2.0+ (from pyproject.toml). Must use BaseModel, Field(), field_validator decorators (v2 syntax). Do NOT use @validator from pydantic.v1. Config must be ConfigDict (not Config class with Meta).

constraint.title: Python Type Hints (MANDATORY)
constraint.description: Use modern Python 3.10+ type hints: list[str], dict[str, float], Optional[T] (not List, Dict from typing). All fields must have type hints. Use datetime (not str) for ISO 8601 timestamps.
constraint.source: CLAUDE.md - Python API Client Implementation - Response Validation

constraint.title: Field Definitions with Field()
constraint.description: Use Field(..., description="...") for all field documentation. Use Field(alias="api_field") for API response mapping (e.g., fixture_id = Field(..., alias="fixture.id")). Use allow_population_by_field_name = True in Config to allow both field name and alias.
constraint.source: CLAUDE.md - Pydantic Field Definitions, data-dictionary.md fixture data mapping

constraint.title: Validators for Data Quality
constraint.description: Use @field_validator decorators for validation. Validate: non-empty IDs, 0.0-1.0 probabilities, odds >= 1.0, enum values (W/D/L, position types, injury statuses), date formats (ISO 8601). Raise ValueError with clear messages.

constraint.title: Config Pattern (ConfigDict)
constraint.description: Use model_config = ConfigDict(allow_population_by_field_name=True, extra="ignore", use_enum_values=True). This pattern established in Story 1.4 (config/settings.py).
constraint.source: Story 1.4 implementation, CLAUDE.md response validation pattern

constraint.title: Module and File Naming
constraint.description: Create 5 model files in /src/bet_bot/models/: fixtures.py, form.py, injuries.py, odds.py, analysis.py. Export from __init__.py. Use snake_case for filenames, PascalCase for class names.
constraint.source: Story acceptance criteria, project structure from story 2.1

constraint.title: Type Safety - Strict mypy
constraint.description: All code must pass mypy strict mode (pyproject.toml: strict = true). All functions must have return type annotations. No Any types without explicit discussion with team.

constraint.title: Linting Requirements
constraint.description: Code must pass ruff checks: E, W, F, I (isort), N, UP, B, C4, SIM. Max line length 100 chars. F401 ignored in __init__.py (unused imports allowed for re-exports).

constraint.title: Docstrings Required
constraint.description: All classes and fields must have docstrings. Use Google-style docstrings. Include purpose, field descriptions, validation constraints, and example values.
constraint.source: Story AC #7, Story 1.5 module structure patterns

constraint.title: Data Freshness Awareness
constraint.description: Models should be aware of data freshness requirements (from data-dictionary): Odds < 1h, Injuries < 12h, Form < 24h. Include timestamp fields. Validators may check freshness or just include timestamp for downstream validation.

constraint.title: Field Aliases for API Mapping
constraint.description: API-Football returns nested JSON (fixture.id, teams.home.id, league.name). Use Field(alias="fixture.id") to map API response fields. With allow_population_by_field_name=True, can instantiate from both field name and alias.
constraint.source: technical-spec.md API integration, data-dictionary.md fixture data

interface.name: Fixture Model
interface.signature: class Fixture(BaseModel): fixture_id: str; kickoff_time: datetime; home_team: Team; away_team: Team; league: League; odds: dict[str, dict[str, float]]; head_to_head_history: list[PastResult]
interface.purpose: Core data structure for a single football match fixture. Used throughout pipeline for data normalization, OpenAI analysis input, and pick output.

interface.name: Team Model
interface.signature: class Team(BaseModel): id: str; name: str; form_5_games: list[str]; avg_goals_for: float; avg_goals_against: float; injuries: list[InjuredPlayer]
interface.purpose: Represents a football team with form data and injuries. Nested in Fixture model.

interface.name: League Model
interface.signature: class League(BaseModel): league_id: str; league_name: str; league_country: str; league_season: int
interface.purpose: League context for fixtures. Nested in Fixture model.

interface.name: AIAnalysis Model
interface.signature: class AIAnalysis(BaseModel): fixture_id: str; markets: list[MarketAnalysis]; analysis_timestamp: datetime
interface.purpose: Output from OpenAI analysis. Contains probability estimates for each market (match result, total goals, corners, cards).

interface.name: Pick Model
interface.signature: class Pick(BaseModel): fixture_id: str; market: str; ai_probability: float; implied_probability: float; ev_percentage: float; confidence: float; recommended_stake: float; suggested_odds: float
interface.purpose: Final output shown to user. Represents a single betting recommendation with EV, confidence, and stake sizing.

interface.name: Models Import Export
interface.signature: from bet_bot.models import Fixture, Team, League, TeamForm, RecentResult, InjuredPlayer, Injury, Odds, Market, AIAnalysis, MarketAnalysis, Pick
interface.purpose: Central export point for all models. Enables clean imports throughout application.

tests.standards: Use pytest as testing framework. Test both valid instance creation and validation error handling. Models must reject invalid data (empty IDs, out-of-range values, wrong enum values). All models must be serializable to JSON and deserializable back. Test Field aliases work correctly for API response mapping. Target 95%+ code coverage on models module. Follow patterns established in Story 1.5: comprehensive test cases with clear test names, test both success and failure paths, edge cases (empty values, None, boundary conditions).
tests.locations: /tests/unit/test_models.py - All model validation tests /tests/integration/ - Integration tests for model usage (after model implementation) /tests/ - Shared fixtures and conftest.py
tests.ideas: - AC #9 (import without error): Test each model can be imported individually and from __init__.py - AC #10 (valid/invalid data): Test valid instances created successfully; test invalid data raises ValidationError with clear messages - Field aliases: Test API-Football nested JSON can be parsed via aliases (fixture.id, teams.home.id, league.name) - Serialization: Test model_dump(), model_dump_json(), and parse_obj() for round-trip serialization - Enum fields: If using Enum for status/result fields, test enum values and string coercion - Required vs optional: Test which fields are required vs optional (with defaults) - Boundary values: Test probability fields (0.0-1.0), odds (>= 1.0), timestamps (valid ISO 8601) - Empty collections: Test how models handle empty lists (injured_players=[], markets=[]) - Nested models: Test nested Team in Fixture, nested MarketAnalysis in AIAnalysis - Validation error messages: Ensure @field_validator raises ValueError with descriptive messages (not generic) - Coverage: Aim for 95%+ by testing all code paths in validators and model initialization
